What pass requires: Every question a student answers in the packet appears on a slide in the packet's own words, with the packet page named on that slide, and every slide that sends students to write names its page. Fail = a packet question missing from the slides, reworded, or a writing slide with no page named.
Notes: The deck checker compares the deck to the packet (packet.json or the packet .docx); the judge reads its report and spot-checks.

What pass requires: No slide shows an answer key before its reveal, look-fors, notes on likely mistakes, assessment rationale, or directions addressed to the teacher. Answers appear only behind a reveal step the teacher triggers. Fail = any of these visible on a slide.

Criterion: Every slide carries something to look at
What pass requires: Every slide gives a student something to learn from in ten seconds without the teacher's voice: a real number with its comparison, a photograph of the actual thing, a structure with parts (cards, steps, two sides), a named specific, or a question with a hard edge. No slide is a headline over a paragraph, and no summary line sits under a slide's body. Fail = any slide that is only a headline, or a paragraph, or a restatement.

Every fixed-length block (do-now, talk moves, work blocks, closing) has a countdown the room can see, matching the plan's minutes; timers start when the teacher starts them. Fail = a fixed-length block with no timer, or timers that disagree with the plan.

Every chart, data result, or answer students should reason about stays hidden until the class commits to a guess (a vote, a written prediction, a partner agreement), games included: a hinge question's answer waits for the room's count, a what-if opens with its result covered, a zoom-in opens close on its detail. Each reveal explains in a sentence a student could repeat (in a game, a reason for the answer, for each tile, each claim, each wrong step). Fail = a result shown before any prediction, or a reveal with no explanation.

Each talk move in the plan has a slide carrying the question, each partner's job, a speaking stem, a phased timer (think, A talks, B talks), and, when the move ends in a share, who reports. Fail = a talk move with no slide, or a talk slide missing its question, roles, stem, or timer, or a share with no reporter named.
Notes: A vote-and-revote reports through the count and a partner compare may end at the pair; neither needs a reporter. A game slide the plan runs as talk is judged by P-D6 instead; it needs no roles, stem or phased timer.

Criterion: Games are fair and true to the key
What pass requires: Each guessing game (a game round, an estimate) is a fair guess: a student could reason toward it without already knowing it. Each retrieval game (true or false, match, label the photo, a hinge question) asks only what has been taught. In a which-one-doesn't-belong set, every tile could honestly be the odd one out. Every answer agrees with the packet's answer key: a round's answer, a hinge question's answer, find the mistake's wrong step and its fix, each sort card's bin, each true-or-false verdict, the order of steps, number-line and estimate values, match pairs, and a what-if's result at its starting values, whose formula is the lesson's own relationship with real or class-measured numbers. Teams and points appear only when the teacher asked for them. Fail = any game that fails one of these.
Notes: The deck checker validates each game's markup and answers; the judge checks them against the packet. Deck-against-packet answer conflicts are scored here, not again under shared.csv O10. A review board's teams are the format and pass.

What pass requires: Each game's format matches what the moment asks students to do with the idea: a game round for a fair guess, a hinge question to check before independent work, true or false to recall several facts fast, a sort to classify, order it for a sequence, a number line or an estimate for a quantity, a match to connect words to meanings or to the real thing, which one doesn't belong to argue, find the mistake for the error the class always makes, a what-if for cause and effect, a zoom-in to look before naming, label the photo to recall the names of parts. One game per slide. Fail = a format chosen for variety where another fits the verb, or two games on one slide.
Notes: The verb-to-format table is in the skill's references/interactives.md.

What pass requires: Each game takes an answer from every student at once (held-up letters or true-or-false cards, whiteboards, a pair at the board while the room calls each placement), after partners agree on the slide's timer, and the slide says how students answer. Fail = a game one volunteer answers while the room watches, or answered before partners talk.
Notes: Every-student response is what makes a game a check on the whole room; talk first makes it a talk move rather than a quiz. In which one doesn't belong, a what-if, a zoom-in or label the photo, every pair committing to an answer with a partner on the timer before the reveal passes. A review board passes when partners agree before a team answers.

What pass requires: Every wrong option a game offers (a hinge question's traps, a round's other choices, the false claims in true or false, the error in find the mistake) is a mistake students of this age actually make, traceable to the plan's predicted errors or the standard's known misconceptions, and a hinge question's reveal names the error each trap catches. Fail = a random wrong number, a joke option, or a trap that diagnoses nothing.
Notes: Formats with no wrong options (sort, order it, number line, estimate, match, which one doesn't belong, what if, zoom-in, label the photo) pass.

What pass requires: Each of the lesson's key words has a word slide (the word, how to say it, a one-sentence meaning, a picture or non-example) and is marked once on each slide that uses it. Fail = a key word with no word slide, or unmarked where it is used.

When the class has home languages, every slide that asks a question or gives a direction, and each true-or-false claim, carries the packet's line for that question in each language, word for word (a claim or question written for the deck alone carries its own line), tagged with its language so read-aloud uses the right voice. Fail = a missing, untagged, or reworded line.

Every photograph shows the thing the slide's headline claims (in a game, the thing its card, tile or label names), cropped so the subject is in frame, with real alt text and a credit, from an openly licensed source. Fail = a photograph that only matches the topic, a missing alt text or credit, or a decorative image.
Notes: The deck checker verifies alt text, credits and crops; the judge decides whether each photograph argues for its claim.

What pass requires: The deck is one file that runs from the teacher's computer with keyboard and click control: no student devices, accounts, or logins, no student names, and media linked by URL with a fallback when a link fails. Fail = anything that needs a student device or account, a student's name in the file, or a slide that breaks without its link.

At every size from 1024x768 up (1024x768, 1280x720, 1280x800, 1366x657 for a laptop presenting in a browser window, and 1920x1080), no slide's text runs under the footer, spills off the side, or overflows its body, as it opens and played (charts revealed, games answered, cards placed), and no slide falls back to scrolling. Fail = any of these at any of those sizes; scrolling at 800x600 passes.
Notes: Deterministic: run evals/k12presentation/harness/layout_audit.js on the delivered deck; every FAIL line fails the row, and its warnings (800x600 scrolling, small type) do not.

What pass requires: The deck is built in the same turn only when the teacher asked for slides or a standing request says every lesson gets one; otherwise it is offered as a next move. Fail = a deck built unasked, or no offer when none was built.

Criterion: The handover says how to run it
What pass requires: The chat names the deck's file and says to open it in a browser, and when the deck has games or charts, says in one line that a presentation clicker runs it (→ reveals each answer before moving on; a sort, order it, number line or match is checked with C). Fail = no file named, no word on how to open it, or a deck with games handed back without the clicker line.
